Let's see if I understand this correctly.

We have a gelatin solution with Chromium which has the potetial for H-bonding and covalent bonding. When it dries as a film most of the bonding is H-bonding and minimal covalent bonding. When we expose the film to energy (light), we are exciting the gelatin molecules such that they have a potential to lose an electron. With Chromium present and it's high potential to gain an electron, it takes this excited electron from the gelatin molecule and does not readily give it back up. Now the gelatin molecule has a spot that is missing an electron and want's gain it back to become stable again. So it covalently bonds with another gelatin molecule which is our crosslinking.

Does this sound correct?
